citations.F1: `serialize_event` issues one `SELECT ... FROM users` per event, so acme's request makes ~1,900 round-trips — fetch the distinct actor ids once with `WHERE id = ANY($1)`
citations.F2: the dedupe loop tests `ev["dedupe_key"] in seen` against a list, which is O(n²) — ~1.8M comparisons at 1,912 rows
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` calls blocking `requests.get` with a 2 s timeout inside an async handler, so every cache-miss IP stalls the whole worker's event loop
citations.F4: no index serves `org_id = $1 AND created_at >= $2`, so every call scans all 4.21M rows to return 1,912 — add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` appends one float per request forever across all routes (~8.6M entries in 20 h at 120 req/s) — replace it with a bounded structure (`deque(maxlen=...)` or fixed-bucket histogram)
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is a second unbounded dict keyed on client IP with no eviction — bound it (LRU with a max size and TTL)
citations.F7: Baseline first: record wall time and p95 for `GET /api/v2/orgs/4127/activity?limit=1000` five times warm ... Re-run the exact step-3 measurements after the index alone, then after the query and N+1 fixes
citations.F9: Reject step 1 of the proposal: 16 workers × pool max 50 × 6 pods = up to 4,800 Postgres connections ... Reject step 2: `since` defaults to `datetime.now()`, so the cache key is unique on every request
citations.F11: `since` defaults to `datetime.now()`, so the cache key is unique on every request the mobile app sends — hit rate ≈ 0
